I know that I can't expect the same exact thing from someone else, but I do think staying in this would be settling, and I feel like I'm too young to spend too much time with this girl if I know deep down I won't be happy long term.

Regarding your relationship ideas of "expecting the same thing from somebody else":

You've experienced an intense "crazy in love" type of experience one time, but those are pretty rare. Don't set your expectations by that example. I once heard a relationship counselor describe it this way when thinking about potential partners and interaction ratios: Talk to 200 people, ask 20 out for one date, potentially 4 might pass muster for a second date, maybe one of those will be worth multiple dates or could have potential to develop into long-term relationship material.

In other words, every "like" or conversation will not become a relationship. Most "relationships" won't last beyond a few interactions or dates. I read somewhere that six months is the most typical breaking point -- not sure if that's true but it sort of fits with my history. Don't expect every a one-or-two date interaction to become a relationship. It's amazing how so many people expect that an initial spark of "hey, I kinda like this person and we have one or two things in common." What you're experiencing is totally normal. It's time to go talk to the next 200 people.

Broken hearts happen to all of us. For the one being "dumped" it is worse to be strung along in an ambiguous state then to get a final decision from someone. Be kind and respectful, and speak from a place of truth. That's all you can do. Pick a good time, not some arbitrary "the sooner the better" -- people are mentally fresh and stronger early in the day, and they will have more options to seek out friends or family to talk to if they need it. Dumping someone at 11PM can leave them feeling bad during a long and lonely night. So, I suggest Saturday morning, stop by her place and take a walk outdoors. It's far easier to stroll away from a park bench than to get up off her couch and get your coat, go to the door, etc. Walking helps people think, too, and in a park or sidewalk someplace outdoors is better than a coffee shop; there won't be strangers overhearing every word you say.
